lead.headline: 189 old campaign funds paid out $8.57M in the 2024 cycle; 19% went to candidates, parties and PACs, not 2.1%
lead.number: $8,569,194.71 out from 189 committees (median $1,794.61); the committee-to-committee file shows 19.4% to candidates, parties and PACs (23.5% with loan repayments), not the 2.1% seen in gifts to candidates alone.
lead.watch_out: The 2.1% came from checking only gifts to candidates; the committee-to-committee file shows 19.4%. The exact-name filter also let sitting politicians' committees (Ted Cruz, Tom Kean Jr) into the list.

sources.quote: Times/WTSP reporters used the FEC’s own data to identify roughly 100 zombie campaigns that have spent more than $20 million since 1995.

Members of the 117th Congress who have since left Capitol Hill still hold nearly $54 million in leftover political money — cash they may tap to make contributions as lobbyists or bank for future runs.

Crenshaw and Linder represent a twist in the zombie campaign story: both converted their campaign committees to multicandidate PACs, rolled-over hundreds of thousands of dollars of leftover contributions, and then used the PACs as slush funds.

Starting in July 2018, the Commission will examine the use of campaign funds by dormant committees as part of its review of campaign finance disclosure reports, to ensure the activity meets the regulatory standards for permissible use.
Campaigns may also financially support party committees and their colleagues who are seeking to remain in office.
